messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a noisy node (gpu-az3-42) during the last canary deploy. Repeated NVRM Xid 79 and some ECC count increments. dmesg is full of lines referencing GPU faults. Thinking we need a tiny, standard 'evidence snapshot' we can run from oncall to collect dmesg/journalctl/nvidia-smi, module versions, lspci, and a short nvml health dump and upload it to the incident ticket. Anyone already got a lean one-liner or script we can reuse?

alex: I have a quick adhoc I run from SSH. Not perfect but useful:
```bash
TS=$(date +%s)
OUT=/tmp/gpu-snap-$TS
mkdir -p $OUT
sudo dmesg --ctime | tail -n 500 > $OUT/dmesg.txt
sudo journalctl -k -b --no-pager | grep -i nvrm -n > $OUT/journal-nvrm.txt || true
sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,MEMORY,POWER > $OUT/nvidia-smi.txt
lsmod | grep nvidia > $OUT/lsmod.txt
/usr/sbin/lspci -vv -s $(lspci | grep -i nvidia | cut -d' ' -f1) > $OUT/lspci.txt
tar czf $OUT.tgz -C /tmp $(basename $OUT)
# then scp or presign-upload
```
Works for quick triage. We should add kernel oops + any systemd-coredump metadata.

ryan: Can we also capture per-GPU ECC counters and GPU serials? For flaky cards we need serial + board id. nvidia-smi -q gives serials but put them in a single JSON-ish block so devs can grep fast. Also include the last 100 nv-hostengine logs if present.

jen: +1 to making this a small tool. Suggest `gpu-shot` with:
- collect: dmesg (last 1000 lines), `journalctl -k` filtered for nvrm/xid, last 2 systemd-coredumps, `nvidia-smi -q -x` (xml) for parsing, lsmod/lspci, kernel version and module versions, /var/log/messages if present
- metadata: node name, uptime, allocated pods on node, GPU ids and UUIDs, timestamp
- output: single .tgz and a short manifest file `manifest.txt` listing checksums and which collectors ran
- upload: signed URL to S3 or a secure internal artifact store with 7-day expiry

jen: rough uploader snippet:
```bash
# after creating /tmp/gpu-shot-$TS.tgz
UPLOAD_URL=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-upload/api/presign?path=incidents/$INC_ID/$TS.tgz)
curl -X PUT --upload-file /tmp/gpu-shot-$TS.tgz "$UPLOAD_URL" && echo "uploaded: $UPLOAD_URL"
```

maria: This would cut triage time a lot. Two operational asks: (1) make the collector safe (low IO, cap output size, be explicit about waiting for dmesg/journal calls), (2) ensure we never log secrets (scrub tokens from env). Also, devs want a small parser that extracts the top Xid lines + GPU UUID -> serial mapping for the ticket summary.

ryan: For safety we should run the collector with `nice` and `ionice` and timeout each command (eg `timeout 8s dmesg`). We should also cap tarball at 20MB and skip copying full journal if it's huge — instead extract relevant grep windows. For automated parsing: `awk` or `xmlstarlet` on nvidia-smi xml to build a 1-line summary: `GPU0 UUID SERIAL ECC_ERRORS`

diag-bot: incident-1234: gpu-shot artifact uploaded by maria — https://artifacts.internal/redwood/incidents/1234/gpu-shot-1749998888.tgz (retention: 7d) :white_check_mark:

maria: Nice. I'll open a tiny PR in infra-tools with the `gpu-shot` script and a README with runbook steps (when to run, what to attach to the ticket). We should also add a short `--dry-run` mode for CI and a `--strict` mode to fail if Xid seen > threshold.

alex: If you want I can help with the parsing bits — will add a small Python snippet to turn nvidia-smi -x into CSV lines for Kibana/incident summary.

maria: Thanks team — landing the PR today. Will ping ops once deployed.
